title: Development of an interdisciplinary registry to identify patient- and procedure-related risk factors for postoperative complications and in-hospital mortality following heart transplantation
summary:
Heart transplantation is the treatment of choice for end-stage heart failure. Despite improved surgical techniques, optimized organ allocation, and modern immunosuppressive strategies, the early postoperative period remains associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Early complications such as primary graft dysfunction (PGD), acute kidney failure, severe infections, bleeding complications, neurological events, and prolonged mechanical circulatory support (ECMO/ECLS) contribute significantly to in-hospital mortality.
While international registries such as the International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation (ISHLT) provide long-term data, detailed analyses of perioperative risk profiles at the center level are of high clinical relevance.
A better understanding of patient- and procedure-related risk factors could contribute to improved preoperative risk stratification, optimization of intraoperative strategies, targeted resource allocation (ICU, ECMO readiness), and a reduction in early complication rates.
Hypothesis:
The study’s hypothesis is that both preoperative patient-related characteristics (e.g., age, comorbidities, preoperative organ function, mechanical circulatory support) as well as procedure-related factors (e.g., ischemia times, duration of surgery, intraoperative transfusions) are independent predictors of postoperative complications and in-hospital mortality following heart transplantation.
Secondary hypotheses
•    Preoperative organ dysfunction and severe comorbidities are associated with an increased rate of postoperative complications.
•    Prolonged procedure-related stress factors, particularly long ischemia and operative times, and transfusions are associated with increased in-hospital mortality.
•    Patients with a higher perioperative risk profile have longer intensive care and hospital stays.

interventions.name: Heart transplant cohort as an observational arm

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    All adult and pediatric patients (<18 and ≥18 years of age)
•    Orthotopic heart transplantation
•    Treatment period: 2006 to 2025
Exclusion criteria:
•    Re-transplantation
•    Combined organ transplants (e.g., heart-lung)
•    Incomplete data sets
